title: Software Engineering EBU6304 - Assignment Grading TA
description: Responsible for grading weekly student assignments, focusing on software design principles, UML diagrams, and basic code structure. Provide detailed, constructive written feedback to help students improve their engineering practices.

title: Software Engineering EBU6304 - Lab Assessment TA
description: Evaluate students during weekly lab sessions. Review their local code integration, environment variable setups, and backend dependency configurations. Guide students through basic debugging processes.

title: Software Engineering EBU6304 - Project Assessment TA
description: Assess mid-term and final group projects. Evaluate the team's application of Agile methodologies, system architecture design, and the quality of their functional prototypes (including UI/UX considerations).

title: Software Engineering EBU6304 - Exam Invigilation TA
description: Assist module organizers in supervising the mid-term and final examinations. Ensure academic integrity, manage student seating, and handle the secure distribution and collection of examination papers.

title: Data Structures EBU5476 - Lab Assessment TA
description: Assist students during hands-on lab sessions focused on implementing core data structures (linked lists, trees, graphs) in Java or C++. Help troubleshoot code, explain algorithmic complexities, and guide debugging processes.
requirements: Strong programming fundamentals in Java or C++
Solid understanding of algorithmic time and space complexity
Patience and ability to explain abstract concepts clearly

title: Data Structures EBU5476 - Assignment Grading TA
description: Grade weekly programming assignments and theoretical homework. Evaluate code for correctness, efficiency, and adherence to standard coding practices. Compile common mistakes to share with the module organizer.
requirements: High proficiency in reading and evaluating complex algorithms
Attention to detail and consistency in grading
Ability to provide constructive and encouraging written feedback

title: Data Structures EBU5476 - Project Assessment TA
description: Participate in the evaluation of end-of-semester student projects. Review project source code, assess the optimization of chosen data structures, and assist in conducting viva (oral defense) sessions for student teams.
requirements: Advanced knowledge of data structures and application architectures
Experience with code review and performance profiling
Strong communication skills for conducting oral assessments

title: Web Development EBU6301 - Lab Assessment TA
description: Assist students during lab sessions focusing on responsive web design. Help students debug HTML5, CSS3, and vanilla JavaScript issues, and guide them in creating interactive, user-friendly web interfaces.
requirements: Strong proficiency in HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript.
Familiarity with responsive design principles and basic UI/UX concepts.
Excellent communication skills to help peers debug front-end alignment issues.

title: Web Development EBU6301 - Assignment Grading TA
description:
Strong proficiency in HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript.
Familiarity with responsive design principles and basic UI/UX concepts.
Excellent communication skills to help peers debug front-end alignment issues.
requirements: Solid understanding of Java, Maven, and Servlet/JSP architectures.
Attention to detail when reviewing backend logic and data processing.
Careful and responsible in providing constructive written feedback.

title: Web Development EBU6301 - Project Assessment TA
description: Evaluate end-of-semester full-stack web projects. Assess both the interactive front-end design and the robustness of the Java-based backend API integrations.
requirements: Experience with full-stack web development and RESTful API concepts.
Ability to assess overall system architecture and user experience (UX) design.
Strong analytical skills to evaluate complex student projects.

title: Web Development EBU6301 - Tutorial Support TA
description: Lead small group tutorial sessions reviewing lecture materials on web protocols (HTTP/HTTPS), web security basics, and deployment strategies. Facilitate group discussions and Q&A.
requirements: Deep understanding of core web technologies and HTTP protocols.
Patient and capable of explaining abstract web concepts to beginners.
Previous experience in peer mentoring or public speaking is preferred.

title: Personal Development Plan - Tutorial Support TA
description: Lead small group discussions focusing on goal setting, time management, and career planning. Act as a peer mentor to help students navigate their academic and personal development journeys. Facilitate an open and safe sharing environment.
requirements: High emotional intelligence (EQ) and active listening skills
Previous experience in peer mentoring or student leadership
Excellent public speaking and facilitation skills

title: Personal Development Plan - Assignment Grading TA
description: Read and evaluate students' personal reflection essays, CV drafts, and career development portfolios. Provide empathetic, constructive, and highly individualized written feedback to help students refine their personal narratives.
requirements: Strong reading comprehension and academic writing skills
High level of empathy and strict respect for student confidentiality
Detail-oriented and consistent in applying grading rubrics

title: Personal Development Plan - Other TA
description: Assist the module organizer in planning and executing large-scale career workshops, mock interviews, and guest speaker events. Manage attendance tracking, student communications, and post-event feedback surveys.
requirements: Exceptional organizational and event management skills
Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and data collection tools
Strong professional communication skills for interacting with guest speakers
